# CodeX Switch

> Parallel multi-account manager for the OpenAI Codex CLI and Claude Code. Each account gets its own CODEX_HOME (Codex) or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (Claude Code) directory; a shell function `cx` picks one per terminal, so several accounts can be used at the same time. Works in zsh, bash and fish. MIT licensed.

Repo: https://github.com/szupzj18/codex-switch
Site: https://szupzj18.github.io/codex-switch/
This file: https://szupzj18.github.io/codex-switch/llms.txt
Full docs: https://github.com/szupzj18/codex-switch/blob/main/README.md

## What it is (and is not)

- One Python 3.8+ program (`cx_core.py`, standard library only) plus a thin wrapper per shell (`codex-switch.zsh`, `.bash`, `.fish`).
- Isolation is done by setting the `CODEX_HOME` environment variable. There is no global "active account", no daemon, no proxy, and no wrapper around the `codex` binary.
- It manages the Codex CLI and Claude Code (subscription logins). The Codex desktop app and the VS Code extension do not read CODEX_HOME.
- Claude Code accounts use Claude Code's own multi-account mechanism: one CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per account (settings, history and the login are per directory; on macOS the Keychain entry name is derived from the directory path).
- It never modifies anything inside an account's home directory.

## Requirements

- zsh 5.3+, bash 3.2+ or fish 3+
- python3 3.8+
- The official Codex CLI and/or Claude Code on PATH (needed for sign-in and one-shot runs)

## Install

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/szupzj18/codex-switch/main/install.sh | sh

This copies the files to ~/.codex-switch (override with CX_HOME) and appends a marked `source` block to ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc and ~/.config/fish/conf.d/codex-switch.fish for the shells it finds. It is idempotent. A new terminal is required afterwards.
Uninstall: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/szupzj18/codex-switch/main/uninstall.sh | sh -s -- --purge` (drop `--purge` to keep ~/.codex-switch). Account data is never deleted.

## Commands

    cx                         list accounts: email, plan, subscription expiry
    cx usage [-v]              same plus live limits (5h/7d windows, reset time); -v = detailed blocks (also: cx ls -v)
    cx setup                   interactive first-run wizard (adopt existing homes, sign in, add accounts, bind a directory)
    cx add <name>              create account <name> (home ~/.codex-<name>) and run `codex login`
        --device-auth            headless device-code sign-in
        --no-login               register without signing in (then: cx login <name>)
        --home DIR               register an existing directory instead of ~/.codex-<name>
    cx add --claude <name>     create a Claude Code subscription account (home ~/.claude-<name>) and run `claude auth login`
        --home DIR / --no-login also apply; --device-auth does not (Codex only)
    cx hook install|remove|status <claude-account> [--dry-run]
                               wrap that account's Claude Code status-line command in a relay that caches rate_limits (5h/7d, claude.ai Pro/Max) to <config dir>/.cx-usage.json so `cx usage` can show them; reads no credentials, original command is preserved, settings.json is backed up. If the account has NO status line, install adds a minimal one and requires --yes (or an interactive confirmation) because Claude Code hides most footer keyboard hints while a status line is configured; remove deletes it again. The installed command uses $HOME-relative paths and falls back to the original command if the relay or python3 is missing; `cx hook status` (no name) lists all Claude accounts and `cx hook remove --all` restores them all (uninstall.sh --purge does this)
    cx login <name>            (re)run `codex login` (or `claude auth login`) for one account
    cx use <name>              set CODEX_HOME (Codex account) or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (Claude account) for THIS shell only
    cx use -   |  cx off       clear the switch (back to the default account ~/.codex)
    cx <name> [args]           one-shot: run `codex` (or `claude`, for a Claude account) under that account, e.g. cx work exec "summarize this repo"; for Claude accounts inherited ANTHROPIC_* / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are removed for the run
    cx bind [name]             bind the current directory (and subdirectories) to an account; auto-switch on cd
    cx unbind [dir]            remove a binding
    cx binds                   list bindings
    cx rm <name> [--purge]     unregister an account (data kept unless --purge or confirmed)
    cx prompt                  print the prompt marker, e.g. [codex:work] or [codex:work:auto]
    cx version | cx help

Account names: letters, digits, `-` and `_`; they must not collide with a command name, and are unique across Codex and Claude accounts. `default` is the built-in Codex account (~/.codex) and cannot be removed.

## Guidance for agents

- `cx` is a shell FUNCTION, not an executable. It exists only in interactive shells that sourced the wrapper. In a non-interactive subprocess (typical for an agent tool call) use one of:
  - one-shot: `cx work exec "..."` after sourcing the wrapper, or
  - set the variable directly, which is all `cx use` does: `CODEX_HOME=~/.codex-work codex exec "..."`, or
  - call the core: `python3 ~/.codex-switch/cx_core.py <command>` (read-only commands such as `ls`, `usage`, `binds`, `names`, `prompt` work this way; `use`/`off`/`bind` write shell statements to the file named by $CX_EVAL_FILE, which only the wrapper consumes).
- `cx use` changes only the current shell. It will not persist across separate tool calls.
- `cx add`, `cx login` and `cx setup` open a browser or wait for input (use `--device-auth` or `--no-login` for headless/non-interactive use). `cx setup` and `cx rm` prompts take defaults on EOF, so they will not hang on closed stdin.
- To list account names non-interactively: `python3 ~/.codex-switch/cx_core.py names`.
- Never print or upload `auth.json` contents. `cx` itself only decodes the email, plan and expiry from the id_token locally.

## Files and configuration

    ~/.config/codex-switch/accounts.tsv   registered accounts: <name>\t<codex home>
    ~/.config/codex-switch/claude-accounts.tsv  Claude Code accounts: <name>\t<config dir>
    ~/.config/codex-switch/bindings.tsv   directory bindings:  <name>\t<absolute path>  (longest-prefix match, per tool)
    ~/.codex, ~/.codex-<name>/            per-account Codex homes (auth.json, sessions, config)
    ~/.codex-switch/                      installed program and wrappers

Environment variables: CX_CONFIG_DIR (registry location), CX_HOME (install dir), NO_COLOR (disable colors), CX_COLOR=always (force colors), CX_AUTO_ACTIVE (internal binding state).
On first run `default` is seeded and any ~/.codex-* directory that already contains an auth.json is registered automatically.

## Behavior worth knowing

- Auto-switch on cd: zsh uses the chpwd hook, bash uses PROMPT_COMMAND, fish uses --on-variable PWD. Leaving a bound directory restores the account that was active before entering it.
- Prompt marker: zsh shows it in the right prompt automatically; in bash and fish it is exposed as $CX_PROMPT_TEXT.
- Output is plain text (no colors) when not a TTY.
- `cx usage` sends each account's own access token to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage (the endpoint Codex itself uses) and nowhere else. If it fails it prints the reason, e.g. "token expired (run codex once to refresh)" or "network error: ... (check proxy)".
- The EXPIRES column comes from the cached sign-in token and can be stale after a renewal (marked with a warning sign); the live limits are authoritative.
- Claude Code accounts: account and plan come from `claude auth status`. Usage windows come from the status-line relay cache (see `cx hook`), shown with their age; they only exist after the account has been used once with the relay installed. `cx use` on a Claude account warns if ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set, because they outrank or redirect the subscription login. Console sign-ins without an API key are stored outside the config directory and are not isolated.
- Not supported: API-key login, importing a token or auth.json with a single command, third-party Claude providers, Windows.
